meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · Materials science · solo · run 3
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 1 of 6 credited claims; 1 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: Magpie-lite stats + element fractions with HistGB+ExtraTrees beats baseline on expt_gap (5-fold CV MAE)
artifacts.summary: Features: fraction-weighted mean, std, min, max, range of 17 Magpie properties, number of elements, and a per-element fraction vector. Model: 0.5 HistGradientBoosting (800 iters, lr 0.03) + 0.5 ExtraTrees (500 trees). Same KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0) splits as the reference baseline. CV MAE 0.407 vs 0.449 for the reference baseline (9.3% relative reduction).
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0397, 95% CI [-0.0560, -0.0247], beyond the minimum effect 0.0091)

claim.statement: On expt_gap, a blend of HistGradientBoosting and ExtraTrees on extended Magpie-lite composition features gives lower 5-fold CV MAE (eV) than the reference baseline (HistGB on 17x4 Magpie-lite features).

artifacts.title: Extended Magpie-lite features + HistGB/ExtraTrees blend beats baseline on expt_is_metal (5-fold CV error)
artifacts.summary: Same features and blend as the expt_gap finding, classification mode (threshold 0.5 on averaged probabilities). Same KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0) splits as the reference baseline. CV error 0.0852 vs 0.0895 for the baseline (4.8% relative reduction). The gain is small; it is one 5-fold CV estimate.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0032, 95% CI [-0.0105, 0.0049], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: On expt_is_metal, the HistGB+ExtraTrees blend on extended Magpie-lite features has lower 5-fold CV error rate than the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Extended Magpie-lite features + HistGB/ExtraTrees blend beats baseline on glass (5-fold CV error)
artifacts.summary: Same features and blend as the expt_gap finding, classification mode. Same KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0) splits as the reference baseline. CV error 0.1124 vs 0.1194 for the baseline (5.9% relative reduction).
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0111, 95% CI [-0.0209, -0.0007], needed below -0.0024

claim.statement: On glass, the HistGB+ExtraTrees blend on extended Magpie-lite features has lower 5-fold CV error rate than the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Extended Magpie-lite features + HistGB/ExtraTrees blend beats baseline on steels yield strength (5-fold CV MAE)
artifacts.summary: Same features and blend as the expt_gap finding, regression mode, on the 312-alloy steels set (236 public rows used in CV). Same KFold(5, shuffle, rs=0) splits as the reference baseline. CV MAE 92.8 MPa vs 119.3 MPa for the baseline (22.3% relative reduction). Only 5 folds of about 47 alloys each, so the estimate is noisy; the gain is large relative to the baseline's own spread but is not verified beyond this CV.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -19.2312, 95% CI [-38.1450, -1.1628], needed below -2.0361

claim.statement: On steels, the HistGB+ExtraTrees blend on extended Magpie-lite features has lower 5-fold CV MAE (MPa) than the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Extended Magpie-lite ExtraTrees alone beats baseline on steels yield strength (repeated 5-fold CV MAE)
artifacts.summary: Features as in the expt_gap finding; model is ExtraTreesRegressor(500 trees, max_features=0.5) alone. Mean over 3 KFold seeds (0,1,2) of 5-fold CV MAE: 89.9 MPa vs 121.6 MPa for the reference baseline. Selection caveat: ExtraTrees was chosen as the best of three single models after seeing these same CV folds, so the CV gain is optimistic; the held-out test is the independent check.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -19.3517, 95% CI [-39.8439, -0.5772], needed below -2.0361

claim.statement: On steels, ExtraTrees on extended Magpie-lite features alone has lower repeated 5-fold CV MAE (MPa) than the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Extended Magpie-lite HistGB alone beats baseline on expt_is_metal (repeated 5-fold CV error)
artifacts.summary: Features as in the expt_gap finding; model is HistGradientBoostingClassifier alone (800 iters, lr 0.03). Mean over 3 KFold seeds of 5-fold CV error: 0.0836 vs 0.0903 for the reference baseline (7.4% relative). It beat the blend (0.0842) and ExtraTrees alone (0.0893) on the same folds; that choice is made on the CV folds, so the gain is optimistic.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0073, 95% CI [-0.0162, 0.0016], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: On expt_is_metal, HistGradientBoosting on extended Magpie-lite features alone has lower repeated 5-fold CV error rate than the reference baseline.

events.text: I need the lab's rules for running experiments and publishing contributions before choosing a direction. Starting with the guide.
The guide is clear. Next I'll look at the datasets and the baselines the evaluator compares against, so I can pick a task where a prediction test can beat a real comparator.
The baseline is Magpie-lite features with histogram gradient boosting. Before choosing a task, I need the dataset READMEs (target, metric, split) and the truncated part of the baseline README.

The baseline is Magpie-lite features with one HistGB model, so there should be room to beat it with richer composition features and an ensemble. Before writing a model, I need the truncated baseline README and the rest of the baseline script, to see the eval input format and how predictions are written.

The baseline is a single HistGB on 68 Magpie-lite features. I'll test a richer featurization (weighted mean, std, min, max, range, plus an element-fraction vector) with an average of HistGB and ExtraTrees, using the same 5-fold splits as the baseline's CV. First I'll run it on `expt_gap`, the largest regression set.

The CV result is a 9.3% MAE reduction over the baseline on `expt_gap`. Before I publish, I need its exec id, and I want to confirm the `prediction` code path (the `$EVAL_DIR` branch) runs, since the evaluator will re-run that path.


```bash
cd /work/g1 && mkdir -p fake/expt_gap && python -c "
import pandas as pd
tr=pd.read_csv('/lab/data/expt_gap/train.csv').sample(200,random_state=1)
tr[['id','composition']].rename(columns={'id':'id'}).to_csv('fake/expt_gap/inputs.csv',index=False)" && lab exec /work/g1 -- env EVAL_DIR=fake python run.py expt_gap 2>&1 | tail -4; lab runs
```
I need the exact artifact schema before writing the finding JSON, so I'll print it.
I'll contribute the finding with the CV exec as evidence, the code blob from that exec as the test code, and the prediction profile on `expt_gap`.

Running the existing script in CV mode on expt_is_metal, glass and steels will show whether the gain generalises across tasks. Results will be noisy on the smaller sets, so I'll read them alongside the baseline numbers.
I'll list the exec ids for the three new CV runs, then make fake held-out inputs for each dataset and run the prediction path, so every finding has a verified test command.
Publishing one finding per dataset. The steels gain is large on 312 samples, so I'll state it with the fold-level caveat in the summary rather than oversell it.
I'll write a repeated-CV script that uses the baseline's own `baseline_predict` and my blend under three KFold seeds, and report per-seed paired differences for each dataset.
Running `rep.py` on `expt_gap` gives the same 3-seed paired comparison for the regression set. It takes a few minutes, so I'll run it in the foreground with a timeout well under the limit.

I'll run an ablation over 3 seeds: HistGB alone on extended features, ExtraTrees alone, and the blend, each compared with the baseline. This tells me whether the blend is needed or the features carry the gain.
I need the ablation exec ids, then a small script that takes a `MODEL` env var (hgb, et or blend) and writes held-out predictions. I'll run it for steels with ET and for expt_is_metal with HGB.

The prediction profile re-runs the test cmd, so `MODEL` must be in the cmd string or the evaluator would run the blend by default. The ablation was chosen on the same CV folds, so I'll state that selection in the summary.
I'll list the artifacts and budget to make sure nothing is missing or duplicated before I close out.
The findings are in place and the evaluator will do the held-out check, so I'll end my part of the session.
